## Load packages

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

## Read and load data

```{r}
FF_genomes_raw <- read.table('../../../Big_data/FlyingFlies_SNPtable.txt', header = T)

# Note: frequency here refers to Reference allele frequency. If freq is low, then alternate allele frequency is high. 
# This is based on the PERL code where:
# (line 56) my $TotalCount = $A + $B;
# (line 61) my $RefFreq = $A/$TotalCount

# N refers to total coverage:
# (line 62) $temp = $temp."\t".sprintf("%.2f",$RefFreq)."\t$TotalCount";
```

## Data cleanup and apply filters

### Create filters for allele frequency and read depth

Allele frequency: #REF suggests a filter of \>3 alleles. This is calculated and filtered.

Ferretti et al 2013 suggest removing all singleton reads.

Read depth: Ferretti et al 2013 suggest that a read depth of 20-30 is a good minimum, and statistical power does not increase beyond a read depth of 40-50. Burke et al. used an upper cutoff of 150.

As of 2026-05-15, read depth filters of min. 20× and max. 150× will be applied.

Gamboa-Santarosa et al 2026 bioRxiv have filtered read depth between 50-500. For allele frequency, they have filtered a combined allele frequency of 1% on both ends.

2026-05-20: Read depth filters of min. 20x and max. 500x. Allele frequency (averaged over all samples) of \<0.01 and \>0.99 are filtered.

```{r}
# filter chromosomes to remove all garbled chromosome names. Set CHROM as factor for easier plotting later.
FF_genomes_unfiltered <- FF_genomes_raw %>% filter(CHROM %in% c("2L", "2R", "3L", "3R", "4", "X", "Y")) %>% mutate_at("CHROM", as.factor)

# make average frequency colum, min. and max. read depth columns
FF_genomes_unfiltered <- FF_genomes_unfiltered %>% mutate(
  mean_freq = rowMeans(pick(starts_with("freq_")), na.rm = TRUE), 
  min_depth = do.call(pmin, c(pick(starts_with("N_")), na.rm = TRUE)),
  max_depth = do.call(pmax, c(pick(starts_with("N_")), na.rm = TRUE))
  )

pre_filter_length <- length(FF_genomes_unfiltered$POS)

# filter allele frequency and read depth (see text above for threshold)
FF_genomes_filtered <- FF_genomes_unfiltered %>% filter(
  (mean_freq > 0.01 & mean_freq < 0.99), min_depth > 20, max_depth < 500)

post_filter_length <- length(FF_genomes_filtered$POS)

filtered_out <- pre_filter_length - post_filter_length
```

## Setting all code chunks below as practice! {style="color: red;"}

## Set up allele frequency data and factors, filter allele frequency

```{r}
# set up allele frequency data as long form data, with each allele frequency having its own row.
FF_frequency_raw <- FF_genome_raw %>% select(CHROM, POS, contains("freq_")) %>% filter(CHROM %in% c("2L", "2R", "3L", "3R", "4", "X", "Y")) %>% pivot_longer(cols = starts_with('freq_'), names_to = "population", values_to = "alle_freq") %>% mutate(Chromosome = factor(CHROM))

# separate each sample name into population ID, generation and sample code
freq_factors <- FF_frequency_raw %>% separate_wider_delim(
  cols = population, 
  delim = "_",
  names = c(NA, "Population", "Generation", "Sample"))

# separate each population and replicate number (a.k.a. line number), convert them into factors
freq_factors <- freq_factors %>% mutate(Population = factor(Population), Sample = factor(Sample)) %>% separate_wider_regex(
  cols = Population, 
  patterns = c("Selection" = ".*", "PopReplicate" = "\\d$")) %>% mutate(Selection = factor(Selection), PopReplicate = factor(PopReplicate))

# set up final data for allele frequency filtering
allele_frequency_data <- freq_factors %>% select(Selection, PopReplicate, Chromosome, POS, alle_freq)

# filter out <2% alt. allele frequency (i.e., ref freq. >98%)

allele_frequency_data <- allele_frequency_data %>% filter(alle_freq < 0.98 & alle_freq > 0.02)
```

## Plot allele frequency data

```{r}
ggplot(data = allele_frequency_data, aes(x = Selection, y = alle_freq, color = PopReplicate)) + geom_boxplot()
```

## Set up coverage data and factors, filter coverage

```{r}
# set up coverage data as long form data, with each coverage depth having its own row.
FF_coverage_raw <- FF_genome_raw %>% select(CHROM, POS, contains("N_")) %>% filter(CHROM %in% c("2L", "2R", "3L", "3R", "4", "X", "Y")) %>% pivot_longer(cols = starts_with('N_'), names_to = "population", values_to = "coverage") %>% mutate(Chromosome = factor(CHROM))

# separate each sample name into population ID, generation and sample code
coverage_factors <- FF_coverage_raw %>% separate_wider_delim(
  cols = population, 
  delim = "_",
  names = c(NA, "Population", "Generation", "Sample"))

# separate each population and replicate number (a.k.a. line number), convert them into factors
coverage_factors <- coverage_factors %>% mutate(Population = factor(Population), Sample = factor(Sample)) %>% separate_wider_regex(
  cols = Population, 
  patterns = c("Selection" = ".*", "PopReplicate" = "\\d$")) %>% mutate(Selection = factor(Selection), PopReplicate = factor(PopReplicate))

# set up final data for coverage filtering
coverage_data <- coverage_factors %>% select(Selection, PopReplicate, Chromosome, POS, coverage) 

# remove <30 coverage depth

coverage_data <- coverage_data %>% filter(coverage > 30)

# Generate log10 coverage (for easier plotting)
coverage_data <- coverage_data %>%  mutate(log_coverage = log10(coverage))
```

## Plot Coverage Depth

```{r}
ggplot(data = coverage_data, aes(x = Selection, y = log_coverage, color = PopReplicate)) + geom_boxplot()
```
